evidence: Cic. Brut. 177: fēstīvitāte et facētiīs C. Jūlius omnibus praestitit (Lewis & Short, s.v. fēstīvitās)
terms.comment: Humour in speech and behaviour, and the jokes themselves. The adjective is facētus, witty.
First charm and grace of manner; of speech, light, pleasant humour, Cicero’s most frequent use (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: good humour, jollity; humour in speech
terms.comment: Cheerful high spirits, and of speech, humour; in Plautus a pet name (mea fēstīvitās). Traupman’s word for humour, with fēstīvus for humorous.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.15.2: Rōmānī veterēs atque urbānī salēs (Lewis & Short)
Hor. Ep. 2.2.60: sale nigrō, biting wit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Sharp, salty wit, often biting; salēs, witticisms.

phrases.latin: est enim lepōrum differtus puer ac facētiārum
phrases.english: for the boy is stuffed full of charm and wit

phrases.latin: sī sēriīs, sevēritātem adhibeat, sī jocōsīs, lepōrem
phrases.english: for serious things let him bring gravity, for playful ones a light touch
